cases.situation: I want to ask my old manager Diane for advice on moving into product management. Haven't talked to her in 3 years.
cases.reply: Hi Diane, I'll be upfront: I'm reaching out because I'm thinking about moving into product management and you're the first person whose advice I wanted, which feels a bit cheeky after three years. I still use your 'write the press release first' trick on every project. If you had 20 minutes in the next few weeks for a call, I'd be really grateful; if not, no hard feelings at all.
cases.note: Name the ask honestly; a reconnect that hides a favour reads worse when the favour arrives.

cases.situation: 大学室友，毕业后五年没怎么联系了。今天刷到她朋友圈，说在成都开了一家书店。
cases.reply: 好久不见，一晃都五年了。刚看到你在成都开了书店，太像你会做的事了，当年宿舍里就你的书最多。店开得怎么样？不急着回，就是想跟你打个招呼。
cases.note: 不用为断联道歉，用一个具体的原因开头，再问一个好回答的问题。

cases.situation: Me peleé con mi amigo Diego hace un año por una tontería de dinero y no hablamos desde entonces. Quiero escribirle sin reabrir la pelea.
cases.reply: Hola, Diego. Últimamente me he acordado mucho de ti y espero que estés bien. No te escribo por nada en especial. Si algún día te apetece tomar un café, me encantaría.
cases.note: No relitigating the fight; if he replies warmly, suggest a specific day within two messages.

cases.situation: 高校のバスケ部の顧問だった田中先生に、卒業以来10年ぶりに連絡したい。自分も今年から中学校の教員になって、部活の顧問もしている。同窓会で先生のLINEを教えてもらった。
cases.reply: 田中先生、ご無沙汰しています。2016年卒業のバスケ部の佐藤健太です。10年ぶりのご連絡になってしまいました。実は今年の春から横浜の中学校で教員になり、女子バスケ部の顧問もしています。練習の最後に先生がいつも言っていた「最後の一本は丁寧に」を、気づけば自分も部員に言っていて、先生のことを思い出しました。先生はお変わりなくお過ごしですか。お返事はお時間のあるときで大丈夫です。
cases.note: 空白には一文だけ触れ、具体的な思い出と近況、答えやすい問いを一つ。お願いごとは最初の連絡に入れない。

cases.situation: I messaged my old uni friend Tom after three years of silence. He replied really warmly, said he's been meaning to reach out too, and that he's now living in Bristol, about 40 minutes from me.
cases.reply: So good to hear from you, and Bristol is basically next door now. Want to grab lunch on Saturday 10 October? I'll come to you, and you can show me whichever pub has replaced the Crown in your affections.
cases.note: When they reply warmly, suggest one specific day within two messages, or the momentum dies.

cases.situation: I went quiet on my friend Leah for about 8 months during a rough patch, she texted a few times and I never replied. I'm doing better now and saw her allotment photos on Instagram. I want to reach out without a huge apology.
cases.reply: Leah, I've been quiet for most of this year and I'm sorry I left your messages hanging; it was a rough stretch and I went to ground. I'm doing a lot better now. Those pumpkins from your allotment are ridiculous, by the way. Could I buy you a coffee soon, maybe Saturday the 10th or Sunday the 11th? No rush to reply.
cases.note: When you were the one who went silent, one line of ownership is enough. A long apology makes her comfort you; a specific reason and a small plan move it forward.

cases.situation: My cousin Aisha and I were really close as kids but haven't talked since our grandmother's funeral five years ago. No fight, we just drifted; she's in Manchester and I'm in Toronto. I saw on Instagram that she ran her first half marathon on Sunday.
cases.reply: Aisha! Just saw your half marathon photos, huge congratulations. It made me think of Nani timing us racing round her garden, and how you always won. It's been far too long. How did it feel crossing the line? No rush to reply, I just wanted to say I'm proud of you.
cases.note: Family drift gets the same shape as friends: the gap named once, one shared memory, one easy question, and no apology spiral.

cases.situation: 林姐是我第一份工作的带教，四年没怎么联系了。她在上海，我在杭州。今天在朋友圈看到她升了市场总监，想发微信恭喜一下，但不想显得像是有事求她。
cases.reply: 林姐，好久不见，一晃都四年了！刚看到你升了市场总监，真心替你高兴。到现在我写方案都还是先写一句话结论，这是你当年教我的。下次来杭州出差跟我说一声，我请你喝咖啡。不急着回哈。
cases.note: 恭喜本身就是理由，不附带任何请求；一个具体的回忆比一句“恭喜恭喜”更让人记住你。
